meta.title: The Stop on the Hill
meta.skill_frame: Literary text: follow what changes for a character across a story.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 4.35 and 3.52 on the two parts (53 and 46 words), 3.96 together. The load is one passenger across two seasons, so the reader holds one change and one cause. That sits inside the grade 2-3 band and below the 4.1 floor, which measures 5.3 at its easiest.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for literary_text 3.1, band 3.1, sequence 2. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A bus driver who stops at an unlisted hill for one passenger, built so the change across two seasons carries the story.
source.avoided: No bus company, town, or fare. No claim about the old man's health or family.

session.difficulty_basis: One change across two seasons, with the cause of the return left for the reader to join.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 45-60 words instead of 100-200. At band 3.1 the text is short by design: two parts keep the session inside 12 minutes and the whole story stays visible on one screen. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The bus to the coast leaves the depot at seven every morning. The driver knows the road well, including the long hill outside town. For years he stopped at the top of that hill for one passenger. The man was old and carried a walking stick. The stop is not on the timetable.
passage.part_2: Last winter the old man stopped coming. The driver waited at the hill for one more week, and then he drove past. In spring the old man was back, standing at the top of the hill with his stick. The driver pulled over without being asked.

items.prompt: Where does the driver stop for the old man?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He stops at the top of the hill.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says he stopped at the top of that hill for one passenger.
tutor_only.tell: The driver stops at the top of the long hill outside town.
help: The sentence about the hill names the spot.
It is the high point of the road outside town.
tutor_only.core_idea: At the top of the hill.
accept_ideas: at the top of the hill
top of the hill outside town
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the bus depot
if_they_say.ask: The depot is where the bus starts. Where does the driver stop for the man?

items.prompt: The stop is not on the timetable. Why does the driver stop there?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. He stops for the old man who waits there.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says he stopped at the hill for one passenger, the old man with the stick.
tutor_only.tell: The driver stops for one passenger. The old man waits at the hill with his stick.
help: Look at who waits at the top of the hill.
The passage names one passenger at that spot.
tutor_only.core_idea: For the old man who waits there.
accept_ideas: the old man rides the bus
to pick up the old man
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the timetable is wrong
if_they_say.ask: The timetable does not list the stop. Who waits at that spot every morning?

items.prompt: The driver waited at the hill for a week after the old man stopped coming. What was he hoping?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He hoped the old man would come back.
tutor_only.correct_reason: He kept stopping at the hill for a week after the man stopped coming, then drove past.
tutor_only.tell: The driver kept stopping for a week after the old man vanished. He was hoping the man would come back.
help: Look at what the driver did before he drove past.
A week of stopping is a week of expecting someone.
tutor_only.core_idea: That the old man would come back.
accept_ideas: he hoped to see him again
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he was waiting for a new passenger
if_they_say.ask: The passage names one passenger at that stop. Who had stopped coming?

items.prompt: The old man came back in spring. What did the driver do that nobody asked him to do?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. He pulled over for the old man.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the driver pulled over without being asked.
tutor_only.tell: In spring the driver pulled over without being asked. Nobody had to tell him.
help: Look at the last sentence about the driver.
The sentence says nobody asked him.
tutor_only.core_idea: He pulled over for the old man.
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he drove past
if_they_say.ask: Driving past is what he did all winter. What does the passage say he did in spring?

items.prompt: The driver never explains why he stops for the old man. What does the story show about him?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He looks after one passenger even when nobody makes him.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The stop is not on the timetable, and he pulls over without being asked, so the care is his own.
tutor_only.tell: Nobody makes the driver stop at that hill. He looks after his one passenger anyway.
help: Look at what the timetable says and what the driver does.
The stop is not on the timetable, so the company does not ask for it.
tutor_only.core_idea: He looks after one passenger even when nobody makes him.
accept_ideas: he cares about the old man
he is kind to his passenger
he is loyal to his passenger
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the company pays him to stop
if_they_say.ask: The stop is not on the timetable, so the company does not pay for it. What does he do anyway?
